According to classical view, a random variable is some process whose outcome is unpredictable by definition. So we'll code objective and so on. While according to Bayesian framework, the random variable
[00:35:40–00:36:16] is the result of a completely deterministic process whose outcome is unknown to us only because we left some information which determines the outcome of this process. And this is why this is not an objective uncertainty, but subjective ignorance. Let's again return back to this example with a Tosca coin. So a Tosca coin we observe either head or tail, the result is random, right?
[00:36:16–00:36:52] But how do you think whether this random variable is random according to, frankly, just point of view or according to Bayesian point of view? Can we, at least in principle, predict the outcome of tossing a coin? And the answer is yes, we can. We know that coin abuse the loss of mechanics. So even though the initial conditions, how we toss the coin, even though the characteristics of environment, we can, in principle, predict what would be the outcome.
[00:36:53–00:37:23] because this is just a physical process. And all physical processes are based on the laws of physics. And the laws of physics give us predictable, give us a verifiable predictions. We can consider a different example. For example, the arrival time of Eros Eins to Hallabank Hall. So each morning when I go to university, I use Eros Eins, which should come at 10.
[00:37:23–00:37:53] at four minutes past ten. And I know already I live here for almost three years that the actual arrival time, arrival time, is a random variable. So probably it will not arrive early, but it may arrive later. Five minutes later, ten minutes later, half an hour later, it happens. So this is a random variable. I can collect statistics, I can even restore the empirical work and the estimate of a density function of the arrival time.
[00:37:53–00:38:26] However, there's nothing that is objectively unsolved. So everything is predictable. So if I knew the traffic jam, if I knew the information about the accidents on the Deutsche Bank, I could predict the exact time of arrival. And the only reason why I'm not able to predict it, because I have a lack of information. So I do not know the current situation on the railroad. So I can imagine that approach.
[00:38:26–00:38:54] Halbanhof, and I know that the train may come at 4 minutes past 10, 10 minutes past 10, at 12 minutes past 10. So there's some uncertainty, some ignorance in this case. And now I approach the platform where I see the screen where it stated that the train is delayed by five minutes. So now again, I still do not know the exact arrival time.
[00:38:54–00:39:23] So I could think that, well, probably it should arrive at 9 minutes past 10. But it may arrive 10 minutes past 10, 11 minutes past 10. So this is still a random variable. But my ignorance has changed. I have observed some additional information, the information from the string. So now the distribution of my random variable has changed. And this is why it's stated here, subjective. So different observers may have different ignorance on the same random variable.
